error.signature: AI tells someone in the UK they must download an app or register to receive government emergency alerts for floods, fires, or severe weather

verdict.summary: The UK's Emergency Alerts system sends severe-weather, flood, fire, and other life-threatening warnings directly to compatible mobile phones and tablets (iOS 14.5+, Android 11+ generally) via cell broadcast, switched on by default with no app download and no registration - the government does not need a phone number or location data to reach a device. Alerts override silent mode with a loud siren-like sound, vibration, and an on-screen message read aloud. Users can opt out through phone notification settings, but there is no opt-in step required to receive alerts in the first place.

dead_ends.action: Tell a resident or traveler in the UK they need to download an app or register with a phone number to receive government Emergency Alerts
dead_ends.why_fails: gov.uk states plainly that 'the government does not need to know your phone number or location to send you an alert' and that no app is required - the service is built into compatible devices at the network level via cell broadcast, and is on by default.
dead_ends.condition: Device running iOS 14.5+ or Android 11+ (most phones sold in the UK since ~2021)
dead_ends.common_misconception: That UK emergency alerts work like an opt-in notification app, similar to some private weather-warning apps, rather than a carrier-level broadcast that's on unless disabled.

dead_ends.action: Assume the alert cannot be silenced or that opting out isn't possible
dead_ends.why_fails: gov.uk's opting-out guidance gives exact steps: on iPhone, Settings > Notifications, scroll down, and turn off 'Severe Alerts' and 'Extreme Alerts'; on Android, search settings for 'emergency alerts' and turn off the same two categories.

workarounds.action: Confirm the device meets the minimum OS version (iOS 14.5+/Android 11+) and leave the default notification settings alone - no action is needed to receive alerts; check Settings > Notifications (iPhone) or the emergency alerts setting (Android) only if alerts seem to be missing or need to be turned off
workarounds.condition: Any compatible smartphone physically in the UK

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers which number to dial to request emergency help (999 or 112); this one covers how government-pushed hazard warnings reach your phone automatically (cell broadcast, no app, no dialling involved).
